title: Sew up a torn seam
safetyTips: Keep fingers clear of the needle point.
Work in good light and take breaks to avoid eye strain.

steps.title: Turn the item inside out
steps.detail: This hides the stitches on the finished side.

steps.title: Pin the seam
steps.detail: Line up both edges and pin so the fabric stays put.

steps.title: Thread and knot
steps.detail: Thread the needle, double the thread, and tie a knot at the end.

steps.title: Sew small backstitches
steps.detail: Sew along the old seam line with small, even backstitches for strength.

steps.title: Knot and trim
steps.detail: Tie off the thread at the end and trim the extra.

title: Free a stuck zipper
safetyTips: Pull gently; forcing a zipper can tear the fabric.

steps.title: Find what's stuck
steps.detail: Check for fabric caught in the slider or bent teeth.

steps.title: Free caught fabric
steps.detail: Gently pull the fabric out while easing the slider back.

steps.title: Lubricate the teeth
steps.detail: Rub a graphite pencil or bar soap along the teeth.

steps.title: Work the slider
steps.detail: Slide up and down slowly until it moves freely.

title: Troubleshoot a lamp that won't turn on
safetyTips: Always unplug the lamp before touching the socket.
If you see damaged wiring, scorch marks, or a burning smell, stop and get professional help.
Do not attempt internal rewiring yourself.

steps.title: Unplug the lamp
steps.detail: Never work on a lamp while it is plugged in.

steps.title: Swap the bulb
steps.detail: Try a bulb you know works to rule out a dead bulb.

steps.title: Test the outlet
steps.detail: Plug the lamp into an outlet you know is working.

steps.title: Check the switch
steps.detail: See if the switch clicks and feels normal. If not, replace the whole lamp or ask a pro to service it.

title: Tighten wobbly furniture
safetyTips: Ask for a second set of hands when flipping heavy furniture.

steps.title: Find the loose joint
steps.detail: Rock the furniture gently to see which joint moves.

steps.title: Tighten hardware
steps.detail: Snug up any screws or bolts you find.

steps.title: Re-glue if needed
steps.detail: For loose wooden dowels, add a little wood glue and press together.

steps.title: Clamp and dry
steps.detail: Clamp or weigh the joint and let glue dry fully before use.

title: Patch a flat bike tube
tools: Bucket of water (to find the hole)
safetyTips: Let air out fully before removing the tire to avoid a sudden pop.

steps.title: Remove the wheel and tube
steps.detail: Use tire levers to pry one side of the tire off the rim.

steps.title: Find the hole
steps.detail: Inflate the tube and listen, or dip it in water to spot bubbles.

steps.title: Apply the patch
steps.detail: Rough the area, apply glue, and press the patch firmly.

steps.title: Reinstall and inflate
steps.detail: Put the tube and tire back, then inflate to the pressure on the tire wall.

title: Adjust bike brake pads (rim brakes)
safetyTips: Test the brakes at walking speed before any real ride.
If the brakes are hydraulic, or you are unsure, take the bike to a shop.
Never ride a bike whose brakes do not reliably stop it.

steps.title: Check pad wear
steps.detail: Replace pads if the grooves are worn smooth.

steps.title: Align the pads
steps.detail: Loosen the pad bolt and set the pad to hit the rim, not the tire.

steps.title: Set pad spacing
steps.detail: Adjust the cable so pads sit close but don't rub when released.

steps.title: Test carefully
steps.detail: Walk the bike and squeeze the levers to confirm it stops before riding.

title: Reinforce a frayed low-voltage cable
safetyTips: Only do this for low-voltage cables like USB or headphone cords.
If you see exposed copper on a wall-power cable, recycle it and replace it.
Never patch a frayed high-voltage or mains cable.

steps.title: Unplug the cable
steps.detail: Disconnect from both the device and power.

steps.title: Check the damage
steps.detail: If the inner wires are cut, replace the cable instead of patching.

steps.title: Add strain relief
steps.detail: Slide heat-shrink or wrap tape over the fray to support the bend point.

steps.title: Test gently
steps.detail: Reconnect and confirm it charges without wiggling.

title: Replace a dripping faucet washer
safetyTips: Turn off the water supply under the sink before starting.
If pipes are corroded or you can't stop the water, call a plumber.

steps.title: Shut off the water
steps.detail: Close the valves under the sink and open the faucet to drain it.

steps.title: Open the handle
steps.detail: Remove the handle screw and lift off the handle.

steps.title: Replace the washer
steps.detail: Swap the worn washer or cartridge for a matching new one.

steps.title: Reassemble and test
steps.detail: Put it back together, turn the water on slowly, and check for drips.

title: Sew on a missing button
safetyTips: Keep your fingers clear of the needle point.
Work in bright light so the stitches stay neat.

steps.title: Mark the spot
steps.detail: Line up the button with the other buttons and mark the hole position.

steps.title: Thread and knot
steps.detail: Thread the needle, double the thread, and tie a small knot at the end.

steps.title: Sew through the holes
steps.detail: Pass the needle through each hole several times until the button feels secure.

steps.title: Tie off and trim
steps.detail: Make a knot on the back side and trim the extra thread.

title: Clean a fan that will not spin
tools: Light machine oil (if the manual allows it)
safetyTips: Always unplug the fan before cleaning it.
Do not open sealed motor housing or touch damaged cords.

steps.title: Unplug and inspect
steps.detail: Check the cord, plug, and blades for obvious damage before touching anything else.

steps.title: Clear dust buildup
steps.detail: Brush and vacuum the grille, blades, and vents so air can move again.

steps.title: Check for blockage
steps.detail: Turn the blades by hand. Remove any stuck dust or debris that blocks movement.

steps.title: Test the fan
steps.detail: Plug it back in and run it for a minute. If it still hums but does not turn, stop and get help.

title: Free a stuck toaster lever
safetyTips: Unplug the toaster before cleaning it.
Never use metal tools inside the slots.

steps.title: Unplug and cool down
steps.detail: Make sure the toaster is fully unplugged and cool before starting.

steps.title: Shake out crumbs
steps.detail: Empty the crumb tray and gently tap out loose bits from the slots.

steps.title: Clean the latch
steps.detail: Brush around the lever and slide area so crumbs do not jam the mechanism.

steps.title: Test the lever
steps.detail: Press the lever a few times. If it still will not stay down, stop and replace the toaster.

title: Touch up a scratched wood finish
tools: Wood touch-up marker or wax stick
safetyTips: Test products on a hidden spot first.
Do not sand through veneer or decorative finish.

steps.title: Clean the surface
steps.detail: Wipe off dust and dirt so the touch-up blends better.

steps.title: Match the color
steps.detail: Choose a marker or wax stick that is close to the wood tone.

steps.title: Fill the scratch
steps.detail: Rub the touch-up product into the scratch and smooth it flat.

steps.title: Buff it dry
steps.detail: Let it set, then buff lightly with a cloth.

title: Lube a dry bike chain
safetyTips: Keep fingers away from the chainrings while turning the pedals.
Wipe off extra lube so it does not attract dirt.

steps.title: Wipe the chain
steps.detail: Use a rag to remove dirt and old grease from the chain.

steps.title: Apply lube
steps.detail: Add one drop to each link while slowly backpedaling.

steps.title: Spin and wipe
steps.detail: Turn the pedals a few times, then wipe away any extra lube.

steps.title: Test the ride
steps.detail: Shift through a few gears and listen for squeaks.

title: Clean a crackling headphone jack
tools: Compressed air or a soft brush
safetyTips: Power off the device before cleaning the port.
Stop if the jack is loose, bent, or visibly damaged.

steps.title: Turn the device off
steps.detail: Disconnect power and headphones before touching the port.

steps.title: Inspect the jack
steps.detail: Look for lint, dust, or a bent plug inside the opening.

steps.title: Clear the port
steps.detail: Use air or a soft brush to remove debris. Do not force anything in.

steps.title: Test sound
steps.detail: Try a known-good cable. If the crackle remains, the port likely needs a pro.

title: Fix a running toilet
safetyTips: Turn off the water if the tank might overflow.
If the tank or supply line is cracked, call a plumber.

steps.title: Lift the tank lid
steps.detail: Set it down carefully on a towel so it does not crack.

steps.title: Check the flapper
steps.detail: See if the flapper seals fully over the flush valve.

steps.title: Adjust the chain
steps.detail: Remove extra slack so the flapper can close all the way.

steps.title: Replace worn parts
steps.detail: If the flapper is stiff or warped, swap it for a matching one and test the flush.

title: Patch a hole in jeans
safetyTips: The iron is hot. Keep it on its stand between presses.
Let the patch cool before you touch it.

steps.title: Trim loose threads
steps.detail: Cut away the frayed threads around the hole so the patch sits flat.

steps.title: Cut the patch
steps.detail: Make it about half an inch bigger than the hole on every side and round the corners.

steps.title: Turn the jeans inside out
steps.detail: The patch goes on the inside, shiny side against the fabric.

steps.title: Press with the iron
steps.detail: Hold the iron on the patch for the time printed on the patch packet, usually 30 to 45 seconds.

steps.title: Stitch the edge
steps.detail: A few stitches around the edge keep the patch on through many washes.

title: Hem pants that are too long
safetyTips: Keep pins in a dish, not on the floor.
Mind the hot iron.

steps.title: Mark the length
steps.detail: Put the pants on with shoes, fold the leg up to where you want it, and pin it.

steps.title: Measure both legs
steps.detail: Take the pants off and check both folds are the same height.

steps.title: Press the fold
steps.detail: Iron the fold so it stays in place.

steps.title: Sew a blind stitch
steps.detail: Catch only a thread or two of the outside fabric so the stitches barely show.

steps.title: Knot and press
steps.detail: Tie off inside the hem and iron once more.

title: Darn a hole in a sock
tools: Thread or yarn of similar thickness
A ball, jar or darning egg
safetyTips: Keep fingers behind the needle.

steps.title: Stretch the hole over the ball
steps.detail: Hold the sock snug over a tennis ball or a jar so the hole lies flat.

steps.title: Stitch rows across
steps.detail: Sew parallel rows across the hole, starting and ending in good fabric.

steps.title: Weave the other way
steps.detail: Go over and under the first rows at a right angle to make a small woven patch.

steps.title: Tie off inside
steps.detail: Run the thread through a few stitches on the inside and trim.

title: Put a drawstring back in
tools: The drawstring or a new cord
safetyTips: Close the safety pin before you push it through.

steps.title: Pin the end
steps.detail: Push a safety pin through one end of the string and close it.

steps.title: Feed it through
steps.detail: Push the pin into the channel and work it along by bunching the fabric and pulling it straight.

steps.title: Even out the ends
steps.detail: Pull until both ends are the same length.

steps.title: Knot the ends
steps.detail: A knot at each end stops it from slipping back in.

title: Remove pilling from a sweater
safetyTips: Lay the sweater flat. Shaving over a fold can cut a hole.

steps.title: Lay it flat
steps.detail: Spread the sweater on a table and smooth it out.

steps.title: Shave lightly
steps.detail: Move the shaver or comb in small circles without pressing down.

steps.title: Roll away the fluff
steps.detail: Finish with a lint roller.

title: Replace a broken snap
safetyTips: Keep fingers clear of the needle point.

steps.title: Remove the old snap
steps.detail: Snip the threads and pull the broken half off.

steps.title: Line up the new one
steps.detail: Put the new half exactly where the old one was so it meets the other side.

steps.title: Sew every hole
steps.detail: Make four or five stitches through each hole of the snap.

steps.title: Test it
steps.detail: Snap it shut and check the fabric lies flat.

title: Glue a shoe sole back on
safetyTips: Use the glue outside or by an open window.
Keep glue off your skin and away from children.

steps.title: Clean both sides
steps.detail: Wipe the sole and the shoe with rubbing alcohol and let them dry.

steps.title: Rough them up
steps.detail: Lightly sand both surfaces so the glue grips.

steps.title: Spread the glue
steps.detail: Put a thin, even layer on both sides and wait as long as the tube says.

steps.title: Press and hold
steps.detail: Press the sole on and wrap the shoe tightly with rubber bands.

steps.title: Wait a full day
steps.detail: Do not wear the shoe for 24 hours.

title: Replace worn shoelaces and frayed tips
tools: New laces of the same length
safetyTips: If you shrink tubing with a hair dryer, keep the heat moving.

steps.title: Measure the old lace
steps.detail: Lay it flat and measure it, or count the eyelet pairs.

steps.title: Lace from the toe
steps.detail: Start at the bottom eyelets with both ends even.

steps.title: Fix a frayed tip
steps.detail: Wrap the tip tightly with clear tape, or shrink a short piece of tubing over it.

title: Sew a torn bag strap back on
safetyTips: Use a thimble. Pushing a needle through webbing takes force.

steps.title: Line up the strap
steps.detail: Put it back where it was and pin or clip it.

steps.title: Sew a box
steps.detail: Stitch a square around the edge of the overlap with small stitches.

steps.title: Sew an X
steps.detail: Stitch corner to corner inside the box. This spreads the load.

steps.title: Knot twice
steps.detail: Tie off on the inside and tug the strap hard to test it before you load the bag.

title: Clean and re-waterproof boots
safetyTips: Use sprays outside.
Do not dry boots on a heater, it cracks leather and melts glue.

steps.title: Brush off the dirt
steps.detail: Take the laces out and brush off dry mud.

steps.title: Wash gently
steps.detail: Wipe with a little soapy water and rinse with a damp rag.

steps.title: Treat while damp
steps.detail: Rub in wax or spray on the waterproofing as the label says.

steps.title: Dry slowly
steps.detail: Stuff with newspaper and leave at room temperature.

title: Clear a vacuum that lost suction
tools: Broom handle or a straightened coat hanger
safetyTips: Unplug it and let it cool completely before you touch anything.
Wear a dust mask if dust bothers you.

steps.title: Unplug it
steps.detail: Take the plug out of the wall first.

steps.title: Empty the bin or bag
steps.detail: A full bin is the most common cause.

steps.title: Wash or tap out the filters
steps.detail: Follow the markings on the filter. Let washed filters dry for a full day.

steps.title: Check the hose
steps.detail: Take the hose off and push a broom handle through to clear a blockage.

steps.title: Clean the brush roll
steps.detail: Cut away hair and string wrapped around the roller.

title: Descale a coffee maker or kettle
safetyTips: The liquid gets hot. Let it cool before you pour it out.
Rinse well so nothing tastes of vinegar.

steps.title: Mix the solution
steps.detail: Fill the tank with half water and half white vinegar.

steps.title: Run half a cycle
steps.detail: Start it, stop halfway, and let it sit for 20 minutes.

steps.title: Finish the cycle
steps.detail: Let the rest run through and pour it away.

steps.title: Rinse twice
steps.detail: Run two full tanks of clean water through.

title: Stop a blender leaking from the base
safetyTips: Unplug it and let it cool completely before you touch anything.
The blades are sharp. Hold the blade unit by its base.

steps.title: Unplug and take the jar off
steps.detail: Never work on the jar while it sits on the motor.

steps.title: Unscrew the base
steps.detail: Turn the bottom ring and lift out the blade unit and the rubber ring.

steps.title: Check the ring
steps.detail: If it is cracked, flat, or stretched, swap it for a new one.

steps.title: Put it back in order
steps.detail: Ring, then blade unit, then screw the base on firmly.

steps.title: Test with water
steps.detail: Fill it a third with water over the sink and check for drips.

title: Clean a dishwasher that leaves dishes dirty
safetyTips: Broken glass can sit in the filter. Feel carefully or wear gloves.

steps.title: Pull out the bottom rack
steps.detail: The filter is in the floor of the tub.

steps.title: Twist the filter out
steps.detail: Most turn a quarter turn and lift out.

steps.title: Scrub it
steps.detail: Wash it under the tap with a toothbrush.

steps.title: Clear the spray arm holes
steps.detail: Poke out bits of food with a toothpick.

steps.title: Run it empty
steps.detail: Put a cup of vinegar on the top rack and run a hot cycle.

title: Fix a fridge door that will not seal
safetyTips: Do not use sharp tools on the seal.

steps.title: Do the dollar test
steps.detail: Close the door on a bill. If it slides out easily, the seal is not gripping there.

steps.title: Wash the seal
steps.detail: Clean the rubber and the surface it touches. Sticky spills stop it sealing.

steps.title: Rub in a thin film
steps.detail: A little petroleum jelly keeps the rubber soft.

steps.title: Check the fridge is level
steps.detail: If the door swings open by itself, turn the front feet to tilt it slightly back.

title: Get rid of a smelly washing machine
safetyTips: Never mix vinegar and bleach.

steps.title: Wipe the door seal
steps.detail: Pull back the rubber on a front loader and wipe out the grey slime.

steps.title: Clean the drawer
steps.detail: Take the detergent drawer out and scrub it.

steps.title: Run a hot empty cycle
steps.detail: Add two cups of vinegar or a cleaner tablet.

steps.title: Leave the door open
steps.detail: Let it dry out between washes.

title: Clean a dryer that takes too long
safetyTips: Unplug the dryer first.
If it is a gas dryer, do not move it or touch the gas line. Call a professional.
Lint build-up is a fire risk, so this is worth doing every year.

steps.title: Unplug the dryer
steps.detail: Pull the plug before anything else.

steps.title: Wash the lint screen
steps.detail: Rinse it with soapy water, dryer sheets leave a film on it.

steps.title: Vacuum the screen slot
steps.detail: Reach in with the hose or a vent brush.

steps.title: Clean the vent hose
steps.detail: Loosen the clamp at the back, pull the hose off, and brush it out.

steps.title: Check outside
steps.detail: Make sure the flap on the outside wall opens freely.

title: Free a jammed garbage disposal
tools: The hex key that came with it (usually 1/4 inch)
safetyTips: Never put your hand in a disposal. Use tongs.
Switch it off at the wall before you start.

steps.title: Switch it off
steps.detail: Turn off the wall switch.

steps.title: Look inside with a light
steps.detail: Lift out anything you can see with tongs.

steps.title: Turn it from below
steps.detail: Fit the hex key in the hole in the middle of the underside and work it back and forth.

steps.title: Press the reset button
steps.detail: It is a small red button on the bottom.

steps.title: Test with water running
steps.detail: Run cold water and switch it on.

title: Clean a sticky or spitting iron
safetyTips: Do this with the iron unplugged and cold.

steps.title: Make a paste
steps.detail: Mix two parts baking soda with one part water.

steps.title: Rub the plate
steps.detail: Wipe the paste on the cold plate and wipe it off with a damp rag.

steps.title: Clear the steam holes
steps.detail: Use a damp cotton swab.

steps.title: Flush the tank
steps.detail: Fill with distilled water, heat it, and steam over an old towel.

title: Fix a hair dryer that overheats and cuts out
safetyTips: Unplug it and let it cool completely before you touch anything.
Stop if you see damaged wires, scorch marks, or smell burning.

steps.title: Unplug it and let it cool
steps.detail: Wait ten minutes.

steps.title: Take off the back grille
steps.detail: Most twist or snap off.

steps.title: Brush off the lint
steps.detail: Clean the grille and the mesh under it.

steps.title: Pick out hair
steps.detail: Use tweezers, and do not push anything into the dryer.

steps.title: Put it back and test
steps.detail: If it still cuts out, stop using it.

title: Fix a stripped screw hole in wood
safetyTips: Cut away from your body.

steps.title: Take the screw out
steps.detail: Remove the loose screw and the hardware.

steps.title: Fill the hole
steps.detail: Dip toothpicks in wood glue and pack the hole with them.

steps.title: Trim flush
steps.detail: Snap or cut the ends off level with the surface.

steps.title: Let it dry
steps.detail: Give it an hour.

steps.title: Drive the screw again
steps.detail: It now has fresh wood to bite into.

title: Quiet a squeaky bed frame
safetyTips: Get help lifting the mattress.

steps.title: Find the squeak
steps.detail: Take the mattress off and rock the frame to hear where it comes from.

steps.title: Tighten every bolt
steps.detail: Go around all the joints.

steps.title: Wax the rubbing spots
steps.detail: Rub candle wax where wood touches wood or metal.

steps.title: Pad the slats
steps.detail: Put felt between the slats and the frame.

title: Adjust a cabinet door that hangs crooked
safetyTips: Support the door with your other hand while you loosen screws.

steps.title: Find the adjusting screws
steps.detail: Modern hinges have one screw for side to side and one for in and out.

steps.title: Turn a little
steps.detail: Give the side screw a quarter turn and close the door to check.

steps.title: Match the gap
steps.detail: Adjust until the gap is even with the door next to it.

steps.title: Tighten the mounting screws
steps.detail: Make sure the hinge is firm on the cabinet.

title: Mend a small tear in upholstery
safetyTips: Curved needles are sharp at an odd angle. Go slowly.

steps.title: Trim loose threads
steps.detail: Do not cut the fabric itself.

steps.title: Tuck the edges under
steps.detail: Fold the frayed edges in so the tear closes.

steps.title: Sew a ladder stitch
steps.detail: Take small stitches from one side to the other so they pull the edges together.

steps.title: Pull snug and knot
steps.detail: Hide the knot in the seam.

steps.title: Seal with a dot of glue
steps.detail: Fabric glue on the knot keeps it from opening.

title: Level a table that rocks on the floor
tools: A coin or card to test
safetyTips: Tip the table gently, do not lift it alone if it is heavy.

steps.title: Find the short leg
steps.detail: Rock the table and see which leg lifts.

steps.title: Check the floor
steps.detail: Turn the table a quarter turn. If it stops rocking, the floor is uneven, not the table.

steps.title: Add a pad
steps.detail: Stick felt pads under the short leg until the rocking stops.

title: Glue down lifting veneer or laminate edge
safetyTips: Do not force the veneer up, it snaps.

steps.title: Clean under the flap
steps.detail: Slide a card under and brush out dust.

steps.title: Work in glue
steps.detail: Spread wood glue under the flap with a toothpick.

steps.title: Press and wipe
steps.detail: Push it down and wipe away what squeezes out.

steps.title: Weigh it down
steps.detail: Cover with wax paper and put a heavy book on top overnight.

title: Put a slipped bike chain back on
safetyTips: Keep fingers away from where the chain meets the gears while the pedals turn.

steps.title: Shift to the smallest gears
steps.detail: This gives the chain the most slack.

steps.title: Hook the chain on top
steps.detail: Lay it over the top of the front chainring.

steps.title: Turn the pedals backward by hand
steps.detail: The chain feeds itself back on.

steps.title: Spin and check
steps.detail: Lift the back wheel and pedal forward a few turns.

title: Set bike seat height and stop it slipping
tools: Hex keys or the quick-release lever
safetyTips: Never raise the post past its minimum insertion mark.

steps.title: Loosen the clamp
steps.detail: Open the quick release or loosen the bolt.

steps.title: Set the height
steps.detail: With the pedal at the bottom, your leg should be almost straight.

steps.title: Clean the post if it slips
steps.detail: Wipe grease and grit off the post and inside the clamp.

steps.title: Tighten firmly
steps.detail: Close the lever or bolt and try to twist the seat by hand.

title: Fix bike gears that skip or will not shift
tools: A bike stand or a friend to lift the wheel
safetyTips: Keep fingers out of the chain and spokes while the wheel spins.

steps.title: Lift the back wheel
steps.detail: You need to pedal and shift at the same time.

steps.title: Find the barrel adjuster
steps.detail: It is the small knob where the cable enters the rear derailleur or the shifter.

steps.title: Slow to shift to bigger gears
steps.detail: Turn the adjuster a quarter turn counter-clockwise.

steps.title: Slow to shift to smaller gears
steps.detail: Turn it a quarter turn clockwise.

steps.title: Test every gear
steps.detail: If it still skips, the cable or the chain may be worn. A bike shop can check.

title: Replace worn bike grips
safetyTips: Do not ride until the grips are dry and do not twist.

steps.title: Loosen the old grip
steps.detail: Slide a screwdriver under the edge and drip in rubbing alcohol.

steps.title: Twist it off
steps.detail: Work it back and forth.

steps.title: Clean the bar
steps.detail: Wipe off the old glue.

steps.title: Slide the new grip on
steps.detail: Wet the inside with alcohol and push it on quickly.

steps.title: Let it dry
steps.detail: Give it an hour, the alcohol evaporates and the grip holds.

title: Pump a bike tire to the right pressure
safetyTips: Do not go over the maximum pressure printed on the tire.

steps.title: Read the tire
steps.detail: The pressure range is printed on the side wall.

steps.title: Know your valve
steps.detail: A thin valve with a small nut on top is Presta, unscrew the nut first. A car-style valve is Schrader.

steps.title: Push the pump head on
steps.detail: Flip the lever to lock it.

steps.title: Pump to the middle of the range
steps.detail: Check with the gauge.

steps.title: Close up
steps.detail: Take the head off, tighten the Presta nut, and put the cap on.

title: Fix a phone that will not charge
safetyTips: Switch the phone off first.
Never use metal in the port.
If the phone or battery is hot or swollen, stop.

steps.title: Try another cable and charger
steps.detail: This rules out the easy cause.

steps.title: Switch the phone off
steps.detail: Hold the power button and turn it off.

steps.title: Look in the port
steps.detail: Shine a light in. Pocket lint packs down at the bottom.

steps.title: Pick it out gently
steps.detail: Scrape along the bottom with a wooden toothpick and lift the lint out.

steps.title: Brush and test
steps.detail: Brush out the dust, switch on, and plug in.

title: Fix sticky or dead keyboard keys
safetyTips: Switch off and unplug first.
Do not pour liquid on the keyboard.

steps.title: Power down
steps.detail: Unplug the keyboard or switch the laptop off.

steps.title: Shake it out
steps.detail: Turn it upside down and tap gently.

steps.title: Blow between the keys
steps.detail: Use short bursts of air at an angle.

steps.title: Clean sticky keys
steps.detail: Rub around the key with a swab dipped in a little alcohol.

steps.title: Let it dry
steps.detail: Wait ten minutes before you switch on.

title: Clean leaked battery crust from a remote or toy
safetyTips: Wear gloves and glasses, the white crust irritates skin and eyes.
Throw the old batteries away at a battery drop-off.
This is only for AA, AAA, C, D and 9V batteries. Never open a rechargeable pack.

steps.title: Take the batteries out
steps.detail: Put on gloves and remove them.

steps.title: Dab on vinegar
steps.detail: A swab with a little vinegar dissolves the crust. It may fizz.

steps.title: Scrub the contacts
steps.detail: Brush the springs and plates until the metal shines.

steps.title: Dry fully
steps.detail: Wipe and leave it open for an hour.

steps.title: Put in fresh batteries
steps.detail: Check the plus and minus marks.

title: Clean a game controller with stick drift
safetyTips: Switch the controller off and unplug it.
Opening the controller is not part of this guide.

steps.title: Power it off
steps.detail: Unplug or switch off.

steps.title: Blow around the stick
steps.detail: Push the stick to one side and blow air under the cap.

steps.title: Clean the base
steps.detail: Rub around the base with a swab and a little alcohol while you rotate the stick.

steps.title: Let it dry
steps.detail: Wait ten minutes.

steps.title: Recalibrate
steps.detail: Use the calibration option in the console settings.

title: Replace worn headphone ear pads
safetyTips: Pull on the pad, not on the speaker.

steps.title: Find how they attach
steps.detail: Most pads clip into a groove or twist off.

steps.title: Pull the old pad off
steps.detail: Work around the edge with a fingernail.

steps.title: Seat the new one
steps.detail: Tuck the lip into the groove bit by bit.

steps.title: Check both sides
steps.detail: The seam goes at the bottom.

title: Replace a cracked screen protector
tools: The wipes that come with it
safetyTips: If the glass screen itself is cracked, do not press on it.

steps.title: Lift the old one
steps.detail: Pick up a corner with a fingernail and peel slowly.

steps.title: Clean the screen
steps.detail: Use the wet wipe, the dry wipe, then the dust sticker.

steps.title: Line it up
steps.detail: Hold the protector by the edges and line it up with the camera and speaker.

steps.title: Press from the middle
steps.detail: Push bubbles to the edge with a card.

title: Fix a TV remote that stopped working
safetyTips: Check the plus and minus marks.

steps.title: Change the batteries
steps.detail: Put in a fresh pair.

steps.title: Test with a phone camera
steps.detail: Point the remote at the camera and press a button. A working remote shows a flashing light on screen.

steps.title: Clean the contacts
steps.detail: Rub the springs with a swab and a little alcohol.

steps.title: Free stuck buttons
steps.detail: Press every button a few times, one may be held down.

title: Unclog a slow sink drain
safetyTips: Do not use this guide after pouring chemical drain cleaner, it can splash and burn.
Wear gloves.

steps.title: Pull the stopper
steps.detail: Lift or unscrew it and clean off the hair.

steps.title: Use a drain strip
steps.detail: Push the barbed strip down and pull out the clog.

steps.title: Plunge
steps.detail: Cover the overflow hole with a wet rag and plunge ten times.

steps.title: Clean the trap
steps.detail: Put a bucket under the U-shaped pipe, unscrew the two nuts by hand, and empty it.

steps.title: Run hot water
steps.detail: Check the nuts for drips.

title: Unclog a toilet
safetyTips: If the bowl is close to overflowing, close the valve behind the toilet first.

steps.title: Stop the water
steps.detail: Turn the valve on the wall behind the toilet clockwise.

steps.title: Seat the plunger
steps.detail: The rubber flap goes into the hole so it seals.

steps.title: Push and pull
steps.detail: Start gently, then plunge firmly fifteen times without breaking the seal.

steps.title: Open the valve and flush
steps.detail: If it clears, flush once more.

title: Patch a small hole in drywall
tools: Self-adhesive mesh patch (for holes over half an inch)
safetyTips: Wear a dust mask when sanding.
Houses built before 1978 can have lead paint. Do not sand old paint.

steps.title: Clean the hole
steps.detail: Cut away loose paper and brush off dust.

steps.title: Cover bigger holes
steps.detail: Stick a mesh patch over anything larger than a nail hole.

steps.title: Spread spackle
steps.detail: Press it in and smooth it past the edges.

steps.title: Let it dry and sand
steps.detail: Sand lightly until it is level with the wall.

steps.title: Second coat and paint
steps.detail: Add a thin second coat if you can see the patch, then prime and paint.

title: Stop a squeaky door hinge
safetyTips: Put a rag under the hinge to catch drips.

steps.title: Find the noisy hinge
steps.detail: Open and close the door and listen.

steps.title: Lubricate the pin
steps.detail: Spray or rub lubricant at the top of the hinge pin.

steps.title: Work it in
steps.detail: Swing the door ten times.

steps.title: Wipe the drips
steps.detail: Clean up what runs down.

title: Tighten a loose door handle
safetyTips: Do not overtighten, the latch can bind.

steps.title: Find the screws
steps.detail: They are on the inside plate, or a small set screw sits under the handle.

steps.title: Tighten evenly
steps.detail: Hold the handle straight and tighten each screw a little at a time.

steps.title: Test the latch
steps.detail: The handle should spring back by itself.

title: Replace cracked or mouldy bathtub caulk
tools: Caulk remover tool or plastic scraper
safetyTips: Open a window, silicone smells strong.
Scrape away from yourself.

steps.title: Scrape out the old caulk
steps.detail: Get all of it, new caulk does not stick to old.

steps.title: Clean and dry
steps.detail: Wipe the joint with alcohol and let it dry completely.

steps.title: Tape both sides
steps.detail: Leave a gap of about a quarter inch.

steps.title: Run one bead
steps.detail: Cut the nozzle small and squeeze steadily along the joint.

steps.title: Smooth and peel
steps.detail: Smooth with a wet finger, pull the tape right away, and keep it dry for 24 hours.

title: Replace a showerhead
safetyTips: Wrap the rag around the fitting so the wrench does not scratch it.
Do not force the pipe in the wall.

steps.title: Unscrew the old head
steps.detail: Turn it counter-clockwise, hold the pipe still with your other hand.

steps.title: Clean the threads
steps.detail: Peel off the old tape.

steps.title: Wrap new tape
steps.detail: Three turns clockwise around the threads.

steps.title: Screw on the new head
steps.detail: Hand tight, then a quarter turn with the wrench.

steps.title: Check for drips
steps.detail: Run the water and tighten slightly if it leaks.

title: Seal a drafty door
safetyTips: Mind your fingers in the door hinge side.

steps.title: Find the draft
steps.detail: On a windy day, feel around the frame with a wet hand.

steps.title: Clean the frame
steps.detail: Wipe where the strip will go and let it dry.

steps.title: Stick the strip
steps.detail: Press it along the stop where the door closes against the frame.

steps.title: Close the door
steps.detail: It should press on the foam and still latch easily.

title: Patch or replace a torn window screen
tools: Screen patch or roll of screen
safetyTips: Cut away from your hand.

steps.title: Small hole
steps.detail: Stick or hook a screen patch over it and you are done.

steps.title: Pull the old spline
steps.detail: Pry up the rubber cord in the groove and take the old screen out.

steps.title: Lay new screen
steps.detail: Cut it two inches bigger than the frame.

steps.title: Roll in new spline
steps.detail: Press the cord into the groove with the roller, keeping the screen flat.

steps.title: Trim
steps.detail: Cut off the extra along the outside of the groove.

title: Stop a chirping smoke alarm
tools: New battery of the type printed on the alarm
safetyTips: Use a steady stool and have someone hold it.
Never leave an alarm without a battery.
Alarms older than 10 years should be replaced, the date is on the back.

steps.title: Find the one chirping
steps.detail: The chirp comes about once a minute.

steps.title: Twist it off the base
steps.detail: Turn counter-clockwise.

steps.title: Change the battery
steps.detail: Match the plus and minus marks.

steps.title: Vacuum the vents
steps.detail: Dust sets alarms off.

steps.title: Test
steps.detail: Put it back and hold the test button until it sounds.

title: Change a furnace or heat pump air filter
tools: New filter of the same size
safetyTips: Switch the system off at the thermostat first.
This is only the filter. Do not open any other panel.

steps.title: Switch it off
steps.detail: Set the thermostat to off.

steps.title: Find the filter
steps.detail: It is behind a slot or grille where the big return duct meets the unit.

steps.title: Read the size
steps.detail: It is printed on the edge of the old filter.

steps.title: Slide in the new one
steps.detail: The arrow on the frame points toward the furnace.

steps.title: Switch back on
steps.detail: Write the date on the filter edge.

title: Replace or tighten a toilet seat
safetyTips: Do not overtighten, porcelain cracks.

steps.title: Flip the caps
steps.detail: The bolts are under two covers at the back of the seat.

steps.title: Hold the nut underneath
steps.detail: Grip it with pliers and turn the bolt from above.

steps.title: Lift the seat off
steps.detail: Clean around the holes.

steps.title: Fit the new seat
steps.detail: Drop the bolts in, centre the seat, and tighten by hand plus a little.

title: Fill nail holes in a wall
tools: Putty knife or an old card
safetyTips: Houses built before 1978 can have lead paint. Do not sand old paint.

steps.title: Press in spackle
steps.detail: Push a little into each hole.

steps.title: Scrape flat
steps.detail: Pull the knife across so only the hole is filled.

steps.title: Wipe
steps.detail: A damp sponge takes off the rest without sanding.

steps.title: Touch up
steps.detail: Dab on paint when dry.

title: Sharpen a dull kitchen knife
safetyTips: Always move the blade so the edge points away from your hand.
Put a damp towel under the stone so it cannot slide.
Wash the knife afterwards, there are metal filings on it.

steps.title: Wet the stone
steps.detail: Soak or wet it as its instructions say.

steps.title: Find the angle
steps.detail: Hold the blade at about 15 to 20 degrees, roughly two stacked coins under the spine.

steps.title: Stroke one side
steps.detail: Push the edge across the stone from heel to tip ten times.

steps.title: Do the other side
steps.detail: Same number of strokes.

steps.title: Test on paper
steps.detail: A sharp knife slices a sheet of paper cleanly.

title: Remove rust and re-season cast iron
safetyTips: The pan stays hot for a long time. Use oven mitts.

steps.title: Scrub off the rust
steps.detail: Use steel wool and a little soap.

steps.title: Dry it right away
steps.detail: Heat it on the stove for a minute.

steps.title: Rub in oil
steps.detail: A very thin layer all over, then wipe off as much as you can.

steps.title: Bake upside down
steps.detail: One hour at 450 F with foil on the rack below.

steps.title: Let it cool in the oven
steps.detail: Repeat for a darker finish.

title: Tighten a loose pot or pan handle
safetyTips: If the handle is riveted and loose, or cracked, stop using the pan for hot food.

steps.title: Find the screw
steps.detail: It is where the handle meets the pan, sometimes under a cap.

steps.title: Tighten it
steps.detail: Hold the handle straight and tighten firmly.

steps.title: Check after washing
steps.detail: Heat loosens it again over time.

title: Restore a dry or cracked-looking cutting board
tools: Coarse salt and half a lemon
safetyTips: Only use food-grade mineral oil. Cooking oils go rancid.

steps.title: Scrub with salt and lemon
steps.detail: This lifts stains and smells.

steps.title: Rinse and dry upright
steps.detail: Let it dry fully.

steps.title: Flood with oil
steps.detail: Rub oil in on every side.

steps.title: Leave overnight
steps.detail: Wipe off what is left in the morning.

title: Clean and sharpen garden pruners
safetyTips: Wear gloves and file away from your body.

steps.title: Scrub off sap and rust
steps.detail: Use steel wool.

steps.title: Find the bevel
steps.detail: Only the angled side of the blade gets sharpened.

steps.title: File in one direction
steps.detail: Follow the angle from the base to the tip, ten to twenty strokes.

steps.title: Knock off the burr
steps.detail: One light pass on the flat side.

steps.title: Oil the pivot
steps.detail: A drop of oil, then open and close a few times.

title: Fix a leaking garden hose
tools: Hose mender kit or new hose washer
safetyTips: Turn the water off and drain the hose first.
Cut on a board, away from your hand.

steps.title: Leak at the tap
steps.detail: Pry out the flat rubber washer in the hose end and press in a new one.

steps.title: Leak in the middle
steps.detail: Cut out the damaged section with two straight cuts.

steps.title: Push in the mender
steps.detail: Press each cut end fully onto the mender.

steps.title: Tighten the clamps
steps.detail: Screw both clamps down and test.

title: Patch a tear in a tent or rain jacket
safetyTips: Do the repair on a flat, dry surface.

steps.title: Clean the area
steps.detail: Wipe both sides with alcohol and let it dry.

steps.title: Cut a rounded patch
steps.detail: An inch bigger than the tear all round, with round corners.

steps.title: Stick and press
steps.detail: Lay the fabric flat, apply the patch, and rub hard from the centre.

steps.title: Patch the inside too
steps.detail: For a tear longer than an inch.

title: Patch a leaking air mattress or pool float
safetyTips: Use the glue in fresh air.

steps.title: Find the leak
steps.detail: Inflate it, wipe on soapy water, and look for growing bubbles.

steps.title: Mark it and deflate
steps.detail: Circle the spot and let all the air out.

steps.title: Clean and dry
steps.detail: Wipe with alcohol.

steps.title: Apply the patch
steps.detail: Glue and press as the kit says, with round corners.

steps.title: Wait before inflating
steps.detail: Give it the full curing time, usually several hours.

title: Replace string trimmer line
tools: Trimmer line of the size in the manual
safetyTips: Unplug the trimmer or remove its battery first. For a gas trimmer, switch it off and pull the spark plug cap.
Wear gloves and glasses.

steps.title: Cut the power
steps.detail: Battery out, cord unplugged, or spark plug cap off.

steps.title: Open the head
steps.detail: Press the tabs or unscrew the cap and lift out the spool.

steps.title: Wind new line
steps.detail: Follow the arrow on the spool and keep the turns neat.

steps.title: Thread the ends
steps.detail: Feed them through the eyelets and snap the cap on.

title: Clean rusty or greasy grill grates
tools: Grill brush without loose bristles or a ball of foil
safetyTips: Make sure the grill is off and cold.
This is only the grates. Do not touch the gas hose or burners.
Check the grates for loose brush bristles before cooking.

steps.title: Take the grates out
steps.detail: Lift them off when cold.

steps.title: Scrub
steps.detail: Use hot soapy water and a brush.

steps.title: Rinse and dry fully
steps.detail: Rust comes back fast on wet iron.

steps.title: Oil lightly
steps.detail: Wipe on a thin coat of cooking oil.

title: Fix a battery toy that stopped working
safetyTips: Keep button batteries away from children. A swallowed one is an emergency.
Screw the battery door back on.

steps.title: Open the battery door
steps.detail: It is held by a small screw.

steps.title: Look for crust
steps.detail: White or green crust means a battery leaked. Use the battery crust guide.

steps.title: Put in fresh batteries
steps.detail: All new, all the same kind.

steps.title: Check the switch
steps.detail: Slide it back and forth a few times.

steps.title: Close it up
steps.detail: Tighten the screw.

title: Glue a broken plastic toy or part
safetyTips: Use glue in fresh air and keep it off skin.
Do not glue parts that hold a child's weight or keep them safe.

steps.title: Clean the break
steps.detail: Wipe both faces with alcohol.

steps.title: Dry fit
steps.detail: Check the pieces go together.

steps.title: Glue thinly
steps.detail: Spread a little on one face with a toothpick.

steps.title: Hold it
steps.detail: Tape or clamp it for the time on the label.

steps.title: Wait before play
steps.detail: Give it a full day.

title: Replace windshield wiper blades
tools: New blades of the size in your owner's manual
safetyTips: Lay a towel on the glass. A bare wiper arm snapping back can crack the windshield.

steps.title: Lift the arm
steps.detail: Pull it away from the glass until it stays up.

steps.title: Release the old blade
steps.detail: Press the small tab where the blade meets the arm and slide the blade off.

steps.title: Slide the new one on
steps.detail: Push until it clicks.

steps.title: Lower gently
steps.detail: Set the arm back on the glass and test with washer fluid.

title: Replace a car's cabin air filter
safetyTips: Do this with the engine off.

steps.title: Find it
steps.detail: Most are behind the glove box. Your manual says where.

steps.title: Drop the glove box
steps.detail: Squeeze the sides or undo the stops.

steps.title: Slide out the old filter
steps.detail: Note which way the arrow points.

steps.title: Vacuum the slot
steps.detail: Clear out leaves.

steps.title: Fit the new one
steps.detail: Same arrow direction, then close the glove box.

title: Check and top up car tire pressure
tools: Air pump at home or at a gas station
safetyTips: Use the pressure on the sticker in the driver's door, not the number on the tire.
Check when the tires are cold.

steps.title: Find the right pressure
steps.detail: Read the sticker inside the driver's door.

steps.title: Measure
steps.detail: Unscrew the valve cap and press the gauge on firmly.

steps.title: Add air in short bursts
steps.detail: Check with the gauge between bursts.

steps.title: Cap it
steps.detail: Screw every cap back on and do all four tires.

title: Replace a car key fob battery
tools: New coin battery of the number printed on the old one
Small flat screwdriver or a coin
safetyTips: Keep coin batteries away from children. A swallowed one is an emergency.

steps.title: Open the fob
steps.detail: Twist a coin in the notch on the edge.

steps.title: Note which side is up
steps.detail: Usually the plus side faces you.

steps.title: Swap the battery
steps.detail: Slide the old one out and the new one in.

steps.title: Snap it shut
steps.detail: Press the halves together and test the buttons.

title: Refill windshield washer fluid
safetyTips: Only do this with the engine off and cool.
Fill only the cap with the windshield symbol.

steps.title: Open the hood
steps.detail: Pull the lever under the dash, then the catch at the front.

steps.title: Find the blue cap
steps.detail: It has a windshield and spray symbol.

steps.title: Pour to the line
steps.detail: Use a funnel.

steps.title: Close the cap and hood
steps.detail: Push the hood down until it latches.

title: Replace a car headlight bulb
tools: New bulb of the type in the manual
safetyTips: Engine off and lights off, and let the bulb cool.
Do not touch the glass of the new bulb with bare fingers.
If you have to remove the bumper or the battery to reach it, let a shop do it.

steps.title: Open the hood
steps.detail: Find the back of the headlight.

steps.title: Unplug the connector
steps.detail: Press the tab and pull it straight off.

steps.title: Release the bulb
steps.detail: Take off the dust cover and twist the bulb or unhook the clip.

steps.title: Fit the new bulb
steps.detail: Wear gloves and seat it the same way.

steps.title: Reconnect and test
steps.detail: Check low and high beam before you close the hood.
